image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a sandy or dirt ground. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a greyish-brown body, and orange webbed feet. It is captured in profile, facing left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellow-green hue consistent with a mallard drake.
The eye is visible as a small dark spot on the green head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and typical of a duck, with plumage appearing dense and smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs are visible, orange in color, and the feet show clear webbing between the toes. The positioning is anatomically correct for a duck standing.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing proper feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers is visible at the rear of the duck.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs, which are common AI artifacts in birds.
To check for edge bleeding between the fine feathers of the neck ring and the background, and to ensure the feet are distinct from the ground.
To assess overall texture consistency of the plumage and detect any subtle smearing or noise patterns.

focus_areas: Boundary sharpness of the white neck ring
Texture consistency of the iridescent head feathers
Anatomical connection of legs to body
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the feet. AI often struggles with webbed feet, either merging toes or creating ambiguous shapes. Verify if the webbing is physically plausible. Also, inspect the transition between the green head and the white neck ring for any color bleeding or halo effects.
